gen-gf-noto-serif-khojki-fs-fira-sans: Big open counters give Noto Serif Khojki its bookish face. Fira Sans follows in a plain sans line of constant weight, with a tall x-height, so the heading's faint wedge-shaped pen pressure stands out against it.
gen-gf-noto-serif-khojki-fs-public-sans: Refined and a little bookish, Noto Serif Khojki carries strokes that never thin out harshly, with horizontals just lighter than the uprights. Public Sans does the opposite job, a hefty sans-serif lowercase with broad, open c and s shapes that hold their ground.
gen-gf-noto-serif-khojki-fs-supreme: Supreme reads crisp and dense, a heavy-looking band of text whose letters stay held open rather than curling shut. Noto Serif Khojki adds stems only a shade heavier than their arms, so the whole stretch of paragraphs feels steady and unhurried.
gen-gf-noto-serif-khojki-general-sans: Noto Serif Khojki is all about its big open counters and its restrained thick-thin rhythm. General Sans then runs one stroke width through every letter, a plain sans with an x-height that fills the line and smooth bends that keep long reading moving.
gen-gf-noto-serif-khojki-manrope: Manrope is approachable sans-serif, with bright gaps at the mouth of each curve and a pen line that holds one width. Noto Serif Khojki, with its faint pull between heavy verticals and lighter horizontals, would feel fussy if made small beside it, while Manrope stays smooth like drawn wire.
gen-gf-noto-serif-khojki-montserrat: Spacious, round and bookish. Noto Serif Khojki does best with its mild thick-and-thin rhythm, while Montserrat, a sans with oversized e and a counters and no hairlines at all, glides like wire under the eye.
gen-gf-noto-serif-khojki-satoshi: Satoshi stands tall and friendly, marker-like. Its soaring x-height meets Noto Serif Khojki, whose soft-pencil thick-thin shift gives the pair a gentle, handmade-meets-clean quality that neither font has alone.
gen-gf-noto-serif-khojki-switzer: Soft, poured ink meets a gently tapered pen: Noto Serif Khojki narrows from stem to joint, while Switzer is a plain sans of wire-like tubes at one width with a tall waist line. Their strokes differ, yet both stay open.
gen-gf-noto-serif-khojki-work-sans: Work Sans is contemporary and sturdy. Noto Serif Khojki does best with a faint nib-pressure variation across its round letters, while Work Sans, a plain sans with bowls that never thin at the sides, does best at holding firm joins and a high mean line.
gen-gf-noto-serif-lao-archivo: Classic and traditional, Noto Serif Lao swells its bowls only slightly and keeps capitals barely taller than the lowercase. Archivo, a plain sans with outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height, would overpower it if the heading were made small.
